claims.text: Engineering a nanohierarchical architecture with spatial composition undulation will promote an in-situ adaptive friction interface.
The engineered architecture will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range.
The untreated alloy has a relatively homogeneous microstructure lacking engineered nanoprecipitates and nano-coupled grain boundaries.
Controlled composition variations can be used to generate a nanohierarchical architecture.
Rapid solidification or an equivalent advanced process can generate the proposed architecture.
The engineered architecture includes nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates.
The wear benefit can remain effective from room temperature to approximately 800 °C.
The friction-coefficient benefit can remain effective from room temperature to approximately 800 °C.
Nanoprecipitates and nano-coupled grains evolve under high-temperature sliding into a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer.
At room or lower temperatures, multiple deformation pathways in the integrated nanostructure release gradient frictional stress in stages.
At high temperature, the dense nanocrystalline glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear.
The glaze layer is lubricious and reduces friction by providing a continuously renewed low-shear interface.
The treated alloy will have a lower coefficient of friction than the untreated alloy under identical sliding and thermal conditions.
The treated alloy will have a lower wear rate than the untreated alloy under identical sliding and thermal conditions.
The wear-rate reduction relative to the untreated alloy may be approximately one order of magnitude.
The untreated alloy exhibits higher friction coefficients and wear rates over the same temperature range.
Benefits will be limited if processing fails to produce the desired nanostructural modulation.
Above approximately 800 °C, phase instability or loss of glaze-layer integrity may compromise the benefits.
Long-term stability under cyclic operating conditions has not been established.
